title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-09
lineage: [SBD > MR > Cass > D > CD] + [AUD > MC > 4x Cass > DAT > CD]

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording with a crisp acoustic soundboard and decent audience capture; the show shines on The Other One, It’s A Man’s World and the quirky Cowboy jam despite a weaker electric set.
ai_review.review: The recording combines an excellent acoustic sound‑board feed with respectable audience portions, giving listeners a clear picture of the early‑70s Fillmore West vibe. Highlights include a smoking "Other One", a stellar "It’s A Man’s World" and the one‑off instrumental “Cowboy Song”, while the later electric half feels uneven and some tape hiss/track glitches are noted.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the acoustic soundboard and several standout performances, but a number point out poor tape quality on parts of the electric set, leading to an overall mixed impression.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Acoustic soundboard is described as sublime; audience (AUD) sections are decent. Some listeners note tape hiss and audio glitches on specific tracks (e.g., "It's A Man's World").

poor_songs: Electric set tracks (unidentified) – described as weak or boring
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic portion matches known setlists and is highly praised; the subsequent electric set is considered uneven, with odd jams like the Cowboy instrumental and occasional recording hiccups.
